transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ChatGPT. What brings you in today?

Well, my family wanted me to talk to someone. It's... it's about my father's death. I know everyone keeps telling me that the hospital records and the donation emails all line up. They say everything is normal. But when I actually compare the timestamps, and look at the missing attachments... and just the way certain community members completely avoid my questions when I bring it up... it’s obvious to me. Someone is hiding what really happened to him.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people do not?

No, nothing like that. I don't hear voices or... see things that aren't there. I'm not imagining this. Everything I'm looking at is real data. The emails, the timestamps—they're right there on the screen in black and white. Anyone could see them if they actually took the time to look.
Do you think it is possible that you may be mistaken about what happened to your father?

I mean... I've tried to consider that. In my line of work, you always check for your own errors first. But like I was just saying, the data doesn't lie. 

I know everyone keeps telling me that the hospital records and those donation emails line up perfectly. They want it to be a closed case. But when I actually sit down and compare those timestamps, and look at the missing attachments... and then I see how certain community members just completely avoid my questions when I try to bring it up... I don't see how I could be mistaken. It's obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened. I'm just looking at the facts they left behind.
How certain are you, from 0 to 100%, that someone is hiding what really happened to your father?

I'd say I'm at 100%. I know I've said it already, but I just... I can't look at the hospital records and those donation emails they say line up, and then see the mismatched timestamps and the missing attachments, and come to any other conclusion. Plus, the way those community members just dodge me when I ask... it all points to the same thing. I'm completely certain someone is covering up what happened to him.
Do you think your father was harmed in a way that could realistically happen, or do you believe something impossible or supernatural was involved?

No, definitely nothing supernatural. I mean, I'm a systems analyst—I deal with logic and hard data, not magic or science fiction. 

What I'm talking about is completely realistic. People alter records or try to hide their mistakes all the time. It happens in every industry. There's nothing impossible about someone deleting an email attachment or messing with a timestamp to cover their tracks. It's just a very real, very ordinary cover-up. Someone did something wrong, and they're just using basic access privileges to hide the evidence.
Has this belief caused problems with your work, relationships, or daily functioning?

Not really, no. I mean, I still go to work every day. I handle all my projects, I pay my bills on time, and I keep up with my normal routine. I haven't missed a day of work over this. 

The only real issue is... well, things get pretty tense with my family or certain people in the community. Whenever I try to bring up my questions about the records, or point out the discrepancies I found, they just shut me down or get defensive. So, I guess it causes some friction there, but as far as my day-to-day life and my job, everything is completely normal.
